blocks.content: Lithification is the process by which loose sediments are turned into rocks through compaction and cementation.

rows: Accumulation, compaction, and cementation of weathered rock fragments
Decomposition and consolidation of plant and animal remains
Precipitation and evaporation of dissolved minerals in water bodies

items: Fossils are almost exclusively preserved in sedimentary rocks, making this a high-yield topic for prelims.
Major energy resources like petroleum, natural gas, and coal are found strictly in sedimentary rock strata.
Exams frequently require classifying rocks into their correct formation types: Sandstone (Mechanical), Coal/Chalk (Organic), and Gypsum/Halite (Chemical).

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Sedimentary rocks are formed by the deposition, compaction, and cementation of sediments over long periods through lithification.
They are broadly classified into three categories based on their mode of formation: Mechanically formed, Organically formed, and Chemically formed.
Mechanically formed (clastic) rocks consist of weathered rock fragments and include sandstone, shale, conglomerate, and loess.
Organically formed rocks originate from the accumulation of biological debris, producing coal, chalk, limestone, and geyserite.
Chemically formed rocks result from the precipitation of minerals from water solutions, producing halite, gypsum, potash, and chert.
